points.quote: In supervised assessments (exams, in-class tests, invigilated practical assessments, vivas, OSCEs), you cannot use GenAI unless your assessment brief expressly allows it.
points.gist: GenAI cannot be used in supervised assessments such as exams, tests, vivas and OSCEs unless the assessment brief expressly allows it.

points.quote: In unsupervised assessments (essays, reports, coursework, projects, dissertations, portfolios), you can use GenAI, but you must acknowledge it. If your course documentation says nothing about GenAI, this default applies.
points.gist: GenAI may be used in unsupervised assessments if acknowledged, and this default applies when course documentation is silent.

points.quote: Your course can set additional limits, and those take precedence – so always read your assessment brief.
points.gist: Course-specific limits take precedence over the default, so students should read their assessment brief.

points.quote: Whatever the assessment, submitting AI-generated content as if it were your own work is academic misconduct.
points.gist: Submitting AI-generated content as your own work is academic misconduct in any assessment.

points.quote: Copilot is the only tool approved for this by the University.
points.gist: Microsoft Copilot is the only GenAI tool the University approves.

points.quote: It is the only tool you should use for uploading lecture materials, assessment briefs, slides, etc, and you must get permission from the staff member(s) who created them before you upload them.
points.gist: Copilot is the only tool for uploading course materials, and permission from the staff who created them is required first.

points.quote: Books, articles and other copyrighted materials should not be uploaded to any tool.
points.gist: Books, articles and other copyrighted materials should not be uploaded to any tool.

points.quote: When you’ve used Gen AI, you should include a statement to make this clear to your marker.
points.anchor: How to acknowledge and reference Gen AI use
points.gist: Students should include a statement telling the marker when they have used GenAI.

points.anchor: How to acknowledge and reference Gen AI use
points.gist: An acknowledgement should include the tool name, version and publisher, how it was used, and what was the student's original work.

points.quote: Including a statement on Gen AI use is generally good practice, but it doesn’t override course guidance.
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: Acknowledging GenAI use does not make a use acceptable if course guidance prohibits it.

points.quote: Gen AI tends to have difficulty retrieving sources: it generates text that looks like a citation. It has no way of verifying whether the source exists.
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: GenAI generates citation-like text and cannot verify that a source exists.

points.quote: Always find and read your sources. Use your reading lists and the University Library.
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: Students should always find and read their sources, using reading lists and the University Library.

points.quote: If you are using Gen AI for language support, then give it specific, limited instructions (check grammar, suggest more academic words instead of ‘A, B, C’): don’t use it to rewrite work.
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: For language support, give GenAI specific, limited instructions and do not use it to rewrite work.

points.quote: There are safe tools you can use for referencing and bibliographies: the University offers training from IT Services in Endnote.
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: Endnote is a safer referencing tool, with training offered by IT Services.

points.quote: If you’re struggling to meet deadlines, remember that you have options open to you: Extenuating Circumstances and Delayed Assessment Permits (DAPs) Information
points.anchor: Gen AI in practice - problematic uses
points.gist: Students struggling with deadlines can use Extenuating Circumstances and Delayed Assessment Permits.
